newsitem.title: UK: Late rally in copper underpins other base metals.
newsitem.headline: Late rally in copper underpins other base metals.

text.p: A late rally in London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices lifted the other base metals by Monday's close, though several traders believed prices would now consolidate ahead of Tuesday's all important stock data.
Benchmark three months delivery copper was last at $2,204, against Friday's LME kerb close of $2,187.
The cash to three months backwardation after narrowing in to $145 earlier flared to settle at $170.
Traders noted a move by the London Clearing House (LCH) to raise copper's cash to three months spread margin. The LCH said the spread margin was raised to $3,750 from $1,875.
This action should deter fundamental tightness from being further exacerbated by speculative activity, sources said.
"It will help to prevent a speculative accumulation on top," one said.
Eyes will again fall on the inventories on Tuesday which are likely to show a small fall. But several traders suggest that copper stocks could start to rise over the coming weeks.

This could help to cap any potential spikes in the market against the backdrop of speculative liquidation, though, substantial deliveries into LME warehouses will be needed to seriously dent the market.
Traders will closely watch movements of stocks into LME Singapore and Long Beach warehouses.

Elasewhere aluminium, in line with copper, moved away from support at $1,500 to settle at $1,513, versus Friday's $1,504.50. It continued to be underpinned by nearby tightness though traders noted a lack of strong physical interest.
Nickel gained $30 to $6,940. LME stocks are expected to rise on Tuesday.
Lead was $4 higher at $709, while zinc settled at $1,082, up $3. Tin was last at $6,120, up $5. Alloy was at $1,355, down $15. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 8075
